rule.title: AWS EFS Fileshare Mount Modified or Deleted
rule.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

es.summary: Se registró en CloudTrail una llamada DeleteMountTarget de Amazon EFS, que elimina un mount target de un sistema de archivos. Las instancias o aplicaciones que dependen de ese montaje pueden perder acceso al almacenamiento compartido.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de CloudTrail con eventSource elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com y eventName DeleteMountTarget, es decir, una identidad eliminó un mount target de EFS en una subred o zona de disponibilidad.
es.why_it_matters: Eliminar un mount target corta el acceso NFS de los clientes de esa subred. Un adversario puede hacerlo para interrumpir cargas de trabajo o como paso previo a destruir datos (ATT&CK T1485, Data Destruction, táctica Impact).
triage_steps: Identifique al autor en userIdentity (ARN, tipo, accessKeyId), junto con sourceIPAddress, userAgent y awsRegion. Determine si usó consola, CLI, SDK o herramientas IaC.
Revise requestParameters.mountTargetId y ubique el sistema de archivos y la subred asociados. Determine qué instancias y cargas de trabajo lo montaban.
Revise errorCode: un fallo (AccessDenied) sugiere sondeo. Una llamada exitosa implica impacto real.
Busque un ticket de cambio, ejecución de Terraform o CloudFormation, o ventana de mantenimiento que justifique la eliminación.
Pivote por la misma identidad e IP de origen en +/- 15 minutos para buscar DeleteFileSystem, DeleteAccessPoint, PutFileSystemPolicy, borrado de backups o cambios en IAM.
Revise alertas previas del mismo principal, como geolocalización inusual, access keys nuevas o inicios de sesión sin MFA.
false_positives: Desmantelamiento planificado de infraestructura o rediseño de subredes o zonas de disponibilidad que elimina mount targets.
Actualizaciones o eliminaciones de stacks de Terraform, CloudFormation o CDK que reemplazan mount targets.
Limpieza automatizada de entornos de desarrollo o pruebas.
response_steps: Confirme con el dueño del recurso si la eliminación estaba autorizada. Si no lo estaba, trate como comprometidas las credenciales del autor.
Contenga: deshabilite o rote las access keys, revoque las sesiones activas del rol y restrinja los permisos de borrado de EFS mediante SCP o políticas IAM.
Recree el mount target en la subred afectada con los security groups correctos y verifique que los clientes vuelvan a montar.
Verifique la integridad del sistema de archivos y los puntos de recuperación de AWS Backup. Restaure los datos si hubo actividad destructiva posterior.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel medio es adecuado porque la acción afecta la disponibilidad sin destruir datos directamente, y con frecuencia proviene de cambios legítimos de infraestructura.

en.summary: A CloudTrail DeleteMountTarget call was made against Amazon EFS, removing a mount target from a file system. Instances or applications that depend on that mount may lose access to their shared storage.
en.what_it_detects: CloudTrail events where eventSource is elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com and eventName is DeleteMountTarget, meaning an identity deleted an EFS mount target in a VPC subnet/Availability Zone.
en.why_it_matters: Deleting a mount target breaks NFS access for clients in that subnet. Adversaries can do this to disrupt workloads or as a step before destroying data (ATT&CK T1485, Data Destruction, Impact tactic).
triage_steps: Identify the caller from userIdentity (ARN, type, accessKeyId), plus sourceIPAddress, userAgent and awsRegion. Check whether the call was made through console, CLI, SDK or IaC tooling.
Review requestParameters.mountTargetId and look up the file system and subnet it belonged to. Find which workloads and instances mounted it.
Check errorCode: a failed call (AccessDenied) points to probing. A successful call means real impact.
Look for a matching change ticket, Terraform/CloudFormation run or maintenance window that covers this deletion.
Pivot on the same identity and source IP within +/- 15 minutes for DeleteFileSystem, DeleteAccessPoint, PutFileSystemPolicy, backup deletions or IAM changes.
Check for earlier alerts on this principal, such as unusual geolocation, new access keys or console logins without MFA.
false_positives: Planned infrastructure teardown or subnet/AZ redesign that removes mount targets.
Terraform, CloudFormation or CDK stack updates or deletions that replace mount targets.
Cleanup of dev or test environments by automation roles.
response_steps: Confirm with the resource owner whether the deletion was authorized. If it was not, treat the caller's credentials as compromised.
Contain: disable or rotate the access keys, revoke active role sessions and restrict EFS delete permissions with SCPs or IAM policies.
Recreate the mount target in the affected subnet with the correct security groups, and confirm clients can mount again.
Verify file system integrity and AWS Backup recovery points. Restore data if any destructive activity followed.
en.severity_rationale: Medium fits because the action disrupts availability without directly destroying data, and it often comes from legitimate infrastructure changes.

positive.description: IAM user deletes an EFS mount target via AWS CLI
Assumed role deletes a mount target from the console

negative.description: Mount target creation on the same service, not a deletion
Read-only listing of EFS mount targets
